feedback: The RM correctly captures the task's soft preference structure. The abstract ordering (u0: nothing; u1: has key; u2: key lost while door closed; u3: door open) respects the environment's constraints: door_open requires has_door_key and blocker_moved, and target_picked_up is only reachable after door_open. Transitions: u0 -- has_door_key & door_open -> u3 handles the (rare but possible via scripted ordering... actually impossible per constraints since door_open requires has_door_key simultaneously? door_open can only turn true while holding the key, and has_door_key turning true precedes or coincides with door_open; the simultaneous transition covers the coincident case) is sound. u1 -- !has_door_key -> u2 captures the drop-key-with-door-closed event; note key_lost fires exactly when has_door_key drops while door_open is false, so u2 corresponds to key_lost (with door already closed). The u2 -- has_door_key -> u1 return transition allows re-acquisition. However, one issue: dropping the key while the door is OPEN is not penalized (correctly, since the task only penalizes dropping when door closed), and that case falls into u1 -- else -> u1 self-loop... wait, u1's else includes door_open, but u1 -- door_open -> u3 is triggered on the same step door_open becomes true. If the key is dropped later while door_open stays true, !has_door_key with door_open true — u1 was exited to u3 already, so u3 -- else -> u3 covers it, unpenalized. Good. If door was open and key is dropped, state is u3, and (u1, !has_door_key) penalty doesn't apply — matches 'drop the key while door still closed' semantics. The FINAL_STATES header is present and u3 is declared and accepting (door open = goal-relevant progress; final task is picking up the box, which is the episode end handled by u4 sink with penalty states u0-u3 for picking the box). Penalizing target_picked_up with -1.0 in all states encodes 'do not pick up the box' — consistent with the task forbidding box pickup. Dense-ish progress rewards (0.1, 0.3) bounded, -0.1 regression penalty explicit for the key-lost event. Predicate-only events with per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events in every state. Accepted.

feedback: `blocker_moved` is misaligned and unsafe: the first generator has an invalid stray clause (`... for cell in [...] if cell is not None and cell.type == "door" for _ in [0]` after a complete `for x ... for y ...` chain yields wrong iteration semantics), and the whole expression reduces to the second scan, which checks for a ball adjacent to any door (`grid.get(x - 1, y)`) in any direction, not specifically the cell in front of the door on the start side `(dx - 1, dy)`. This may count balls on the wrong side of the door. Use exactly the code-notes expression: `not any(c is not None and c.type == "ball" for c in [env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)])` with `(dx, dy)` located by scanning for the door. The other four propositions (`has_door_key`, `door_open`, `target_picked_up`, `key_lost`) match the documented expressions and semantics: persistent state readings, event reading via `previous_valuation` for `key_lost` with `not D` requiring the door closed, no extra predicates, no imports, no mutation. Rejecting solely because of `blocker_moved`.

`blocker_moved` is incorrect. The candidate returns True when no door exists (not the case here), and more importantly when a door exists it uses `dx-1, dy` where `dx`/`dy` are loop variables of the *door-scan* generator, not the found door's cell — this is a NameError/incorrect semantics; the condition `not any(ball at dx-1,dy)` is evaluated against an unbound/loop-carried variable pair from the scan, not the door's cell. The documented definition is simply: no ball at the door-adjacent cell (ball in hand counts as moved, so `not any(... at (dx-1, dy))` suffices — no `env.carrying` ball check needed since a carried ball isn't on the grid). Rewrite `blocker_moved` to first find the door cell by scanning the grid, then check that cell. All other predicates (`has_door_key`, `door_open`, `target_picked_up`, `key_lost`) match the documented expressions exactly; `key_lost` correctly reads the previous valuation as a read-only event comparison with no mutation.
